publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Changes in statistical learning across development

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: prediction
span.quote: Reviewing related behavioural and neural evidence, we posited that infants and young children might have broader and less-filtered access to the statistical structure present in their learning environments and that what they represent after statistical learning might shift with age.

span.label: development of statistical learning
span.quote: Discovering whether and how statistical learning changes with development is likely to inform long-standing questions about why children excel relative to adults in some areas, such as learning language16 and solving problems that require unconventional solutions17,18.

span.label: review
span.quote: In this Review, we first synthesize empirical work on the development of statistical learning, which indicates that it improves with development only for certain forms of input.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: faster forgetting in infancy strips away the idiosyncratic details of individual experiences, so what accumulates is a general, fuzzy representation of the commonalities
span.quote: Thus, faster forgetting — and greater forgetting between experiences — can produce fuzzy, general representations (Fig. 5).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: immature selective attention leaves children unable to filter their input, which widens the pool of structure available for statistical learning
span.quote: Because children cannot use attention to filter their experience as well as adults, they can potentially learn more about the parts of experience that adults exclude for being outside their narrower focus of attention.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: attention gates statistical learning in adults, so a narrower adult attentional focus means less input is eligible to be learned at any moment
span.quote: Attention can gate10,81 statistical learning in adults such that unattended aspects of an environment are not always learned.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: children's distributed attention makes them sample many structures at once, trading speed of learning any single structure for knowledge of relationships between structures
span.quote: In a complex environment with multiple structures, infants and children might therefore spend more time learning from multiple sources at once, slowing their learning of any given structure, but also potentially bolstering their knowledge of possible relationships among different sources of structure.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the early-maturing monosynaptic hippocampal pathway extracts regularities across many similar experiences and therefore yields fuzzy rather than specific representations
span.quote: The early-developing monosynaptic pathway is thought to learn regularities from many similar experiences, yielding fuzzy representations in humans and monkeys alike78.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: prior knowledge blocks learning of conflicting structure, so accumulated experience narrows what a learner can pick up
span.quote: In adults, knowledge seems to impact statistical learning: adults fail to learn structures that conflict with their previous knowledge.

span.label: The paper's proposed developmental account is speculative and not yet tested.
span.quote: Although this discussion builds on previous observations about developmental changes in statistical learning, it is largely speculative and remains to be tested.

span.label: The developmental neuroimaging base is too thin to support conclusions about shifting neural substrates.
span.quote: However, a confident appraisal of potential developmental shifts in the neural structures that are involved in statistical learning cannot be made from just two studies that have measured the function of specific brain regions.

span.label: The developmental timelines invoked come from animal histology and general memory research, not from human statistical-learning data.
span.quote: Much of the data on these exact timelines come from histological studies in animals and behavioural human memory development research, so these possibilities for statistical learning require confirmation in human infants.

span.label: The review adopts one of two competing conceptualizations of its subject and says which it rejects.
span.quote: Although some definitions conceptualize statistical learning as a singular and inherently implicit learning system185, we favour the conceptualization of statistical learning as supported by a set of learning processes

span.label: A category boundary is drawn by how the excluded thing is typically assessed.
span.quote: We exclude motor-based skill learning (such as serial reaction time tasks) from statistical learning, because it is typically assessed in tasks that provide external feedback

span.label: The quantity being compared across ages may itself differ by age.
span.quote: However, this availability does not necessarily mean that statistical learning is age-invariant15. Indeed, statistical learning likely changes in quality with age, operating over different sources of data and producing different representations

span.label: statistical learning
span.quote: In this Review we define statistical learning as the learning of structure from repeated exposure to environmental statistics

span.label: skill learning
span.quote: We exclude motor-based skill learning (such as serial reaction time tasks) from statistical learning, because it is typically assessed in tasks that provide external feedback

span.label: serial reaction time tasks
span.quote: We exclude motor-based skill learning (such as serial reaction time tasks) from statistical learning, because it is typically assessed in tasks that provide external feedback

span.label: external feedback
span.quote: Similar to others19, we further require that learning occurs without reinforcement or external feedback

span.label: implicit learning
span.quote: Attention likely plays a role in statistical learning10,81–83 and there is large conceptual overlap with other implicit learning processes

span.label: statistical learning - STIPULATED IN A BOX, WITH AN ADDED REQUIREMENT: defined as the learning of structure from repeated exposure to environmental statistics, with the further requirement that learning occur without reinforcement or external feedback - so the absence of feedback is part of the definition rather than a feature of the phenomenon
span.quote: Similar to others19, we further require that learning occurs without reinforcement or external feedback

span.label: statistical learning - A SET OF PROCESSES, NOT A SINGLE IMPLICIT SYSTEM: the review names the rival conceptualization - a singular and inherently implicit learning system - and takes the other, under which some of the processes can result in conscious access; whether the term denotes one thing or several decides whether results from different tasks can be pooled
span.quote: Although some definitions conceptualize statistical learning as a singular and inherently implicit learning system185, we favour the conceptualization of statistical learning as supported by a set of learning processes

span.label: the exclusion of skill learning - A BOUNDARY MADE OF AN ASSAY: motor-based skill learning is put outside the category because it is TYPICALLY ASSESSED in tasks that provide external feedback, so the same phenomenon assessed without feedback would fall inside, and the hedge 'typically' is the authors' own
span.quote: We exclude motor-based skill learning (such as serial reaction time tasks) from statistical learning, because it is typically assessed in tasks that provide external feedback

span.label: builds-on → previous work arguing that children's advantage in language learning stems from their ongoing cognitive development (refs 16, 171, 172)
span.quote: Regarding language, we join previous work that suggests that children’s prowess in language learning has to do with their ongoing cognitive development16,171,172.

span.label: contradicts → definitions treating statistical learning as a singular, inherently implicit learning system (ref 185)
span.quote: Although some definitions conceptualize statistical learning as a singular and inherently implicit learning system185, we favour the conceptualization of statistical learning as supported by a set of learning processes, some of which can result in conscious access to learning20,21,34.

span.label: skill learning —distinct-from→ statistical learning
span.quote: We exclude motor-based skill learning (such as serial reaction time tasks) from statistical learning, because it is typically assessed in tasks that provide external feedback

span.label: serial reaction time tasks —is-a→ skill learning
span.quote: We exclude motor-based skill learning (such as serial reaction time tasks) from statistical learning, because it is typically assessed in tasks that provide external feedback

span.label: Indirect measures such as saccade latency and neural entrainment show essentially no developmental change in statistical learning.
span.quote: Indirect measures suggest that statistical learning changes little or not at all with development.

span.label: Direct measures such as two-alternative forced-choice tests do show age-related improvement, so the answer to whether statistical learning develops depends on how it is measured.
span.quote: By contrast, direct measures suggest developmental change in statistical learning ability.

span.label: The improvement with age is domain-specific: visual and non-linguistic auditory statistical learning improve across childhood while learning of aurally presented syllables does not.
span.quote: A comparison of the developmental trajectories of visual and aural-syllable statistical learning in separate groups of children aged from 5 to 12 years found age-related improvement in visual but not aural-syllable statistical learning performance23.

span.label: The review's central synthesis is that the format of what is learned changes with age, from fuzzy in infancy to specific in early childhood to broad-plus-specific later.
span.quote: Taken together, these data provide preliminary support for the idea that representations that are formed after statistical learning shift with development: being fuzzy in infancy, highly specific in early childhood, and then increasingly broad in later childhood and adulthood.

span.label: Developmental studies implicate hippocampus and prefrontal regions but conspicuously fail to implicate the sensory cortices and basal ganglia that dominate adult statistical learning findings.
span.quote: Conspicuously missing from the list of regions underpinning statistical learning during infancy and childhood are sensory cortices and, often, the basal ganglia.

span.label: The developmental neuroimaging evidence base is extremely thin, resting on a single infant functional imaging study.
span.quote: There is just one functional neuroimaging study in infants, which implicates the hippocampus and medial prefrontal cortex in visual statistical learning52.

span.label: Overall the review concludes that the two domains follow different trajectories and that this divergence appears only on direct measures.
span.quote: Our review of the development of statistical learning revealed different developmental trajectories in linguistic and non-linguistic domains, with non-linguistic auditory and visual statistical learning improving across childhood whereas linguistic (specifically aurally presented syllables) learning does not change.

span.label: statistical learning
span.quote: We define statistical learning as the learning of structure — for example, frequency, probabilities, or mutual information — from repeated exposure to environmental statistics19–21 that occurs with no explicit instruction or external feedback (Box 1).

span.label: fuzzy representations
span.quote: The first type of general representation might emerge in infancy and could be due to neural maturation or forgetting130; we refer to the resulting representations as fuzzy.

span.label: broad representations
span.quote: The second type of general representation might emerge later in childhood123,131,132, reflect commonalties across events and experiences, and exist alongside specific information; we refer to the resulting representations as broad.

span.label: neural entrainment
span.quote: In another indirect measure known as ‘neural entrainment’, largescale electrical oscillations in the brain are measured to determine their synchrony to the rhythm of structured stimuli.

span.label: indirect measures of statistical learning
span.quote: Learning on indirect measures is inferred without overt report from the participants33 (Fig. 2b) and can be used to measure learning during the learning process itself.

span.label: 0–24 months / 2–7 years / 7–10 years / 18–35 years — the four developmental brackets the review uses to organize the literature
span.quote: In this Review, we consider statistical learning across a broad range of development, including infants (0–24 months old), young children (2–7 years old), older children (7–10 years old), and young adults (typically 18–35 years old).

span.label: one of four — how many developmental statistical learning studies found basal ganglia involvement
span.quote: has been observed in only one50 of four statistical learning studies with infants or children31,45,52

span.label: 18–24 months — estimated age at which the trisynaptic hippocampal pathway supporting specific memories emerges in humans
span.quote: The trisynaptic pathway of the hippocampus — which yields rapid encoding of specific memories — is not thought to emerge in humans until around 18–24 months of age, in the shift from infancy to young childhood143,145.

span.label: 5–7 vs 8–9 years — the age split at which children move from remembering only specific transitions to remembering both broad groups and specific transitions
span.quote: Children 5–7 years old showed memory for the specific transitions but not the broad groups, whereas 8–9 year olds and adults remembered both broad and specific information165.

span.label: 8-month-old — age at which infants were shown to represent statistical input as chunks rather than as specific transitional probabilities
span.quote: For instance, 8-month-old infants represent their statistical experiences in ‘chunks’ (general groupings), instead of as specific transitional probabilities between items133 as adults have been shown to do163.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1038/s44159-023-00157-0.
